title: Excel Canvas offers to turn your workbook into the boss's next report
key_facts: Microsoft plans to roll out Excel Canvas through October, adding Copilot-generated reports to Excel.
Microsoft says Canvas turns workbook data into a polished report with visualisations, metrics and insights.
The reports refresh automatically when the underlying data changes.
Users need access to Copilot in Excel and can adjust the reports with natural-language prompts.
Last week Microsoft added an opt-in Excel feature allowing multiple values in one cell, which could complicate third-party tools.

The Register notes Microsoft dropped the COPILOT() function in August 2026, about 12 months after launching it, and earlier this year made a disliked Copilot button movable to the toolbar after user complaints.
The Register says Canvas enters a crowded market and that businesses already using dashboard tools will need a reason to add another.
quote_evidence: Microsoft plans to roll out Excel Canvas through October, adding Copilot-generated reports to its veteran spreadsheet.
Excel Canvas "transforms workbook data into a polished report containing visualizations, metrics, and insights," said Microsoft.
The reports automatically refresh as the underlying data changes.
why_it_matters_hint: Copilot could draft recurring spreadsheet reports for office workers, but its usefulness depends on whether it picks sensible charts and metrics.
event_date: Not stated; The Register published it on 2 Oct 2026.
notes: The Register's text is opinionated in places; only facts and clearly attributed Register remarks were used. No exact rollout dates beyond 'through October'.
